docs.title: mossyforest
docs.text:
Network aware stable feature selection via Shapley values and random forests.

mossyforest is the Python implementation of the mossyforest R package. It is a bit-exact replica of the R algorithm (verified, see Parity). It is recommended to use this package for large high dimensional data sets.

It selects a small, stable set of features from high-dimensional, correlated data by combining:

  1. Module stratified screening: recursive feature elimination (RFE) within each correlated module (or WGCNA-derived module).
  2. Shadow stability selection: Boruta style subsample selection where each feature must beat its own permuted "shadow" across many resamples.
  3. A single TreeSHAP pass on the stable set for importance, confidence intervals, and a pairwise interaction matrix.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install mossyforest

Optional extras:

# PyWGCNA, only needed for wmf() and detect_modules()
pip install "mossyforest[wgcna]"

# numba and fasttreeshap (fasttreeshap needs Python 3.11 or lower)
pip install "mossyforest[fast]"

From a clone, for development:

pip install -e .
pip install -e ".[wgcna]"   # PyWGCNA
pip install -e ".[fast]"    # numba and fasttreeshap
pip install -e ".[dev]"     # test and lint tooling

Requires Python ≥3.9, numpy, pandas, scikit-learn, shap. Module detection (wmf) additionally needs PyWGCNA, which is an optional extra: pip install "mossyforest[wgcna]".

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from mossyforest import mf, screen_control, select_control

# X: samples x features (DataFrame keeps feature names); y: int/bool = classification
res = mf(
    X, y,
    module_membership = {"gene1": "M1", "gene2": "M1", "gene3": "M2", ...},
    screen_params = screen_control(),      # Phase 1 defaults
    select_params = select_control(),      # Phase 2 defaults
    num_processors = 4,                    # parallel replicates/modules
    seed = 42,
)

print(res)                                 # stable features + SHAP + stability
res.final_SHAP                             # DataFrame: importance, 95% CIs, freq
res.predict(X_new)                         # predict from the final RF
res.detect_interaction(thresh=0.01)        # pairwise TreeSHAP interactions

docs.title: With automatic WGCNA module detection
docs.text:
from mossyforest import wmf, WGCNA_control
res = wmf(X, y, WGCNA_params=WGCNA_control(power=6, min_features=20))
res.WGCNA_object                           # raw module labels

docs.title: sklearn-compatible estimator
docs.text:
from mossyforest import MossyForest
model = MossyForest(n_jobs=4, random_state=42)
model.fit(X, y, module_membership=mm)
model.transform(X)          # X reduced to stable features
model.predict(X_new)

docs.title: Plots
docs.text:
from mossyforest import (
    plot_importance, plot_waterfall, plot_force, plot_stability,
    plot_stability_elbow, plot_potential_interactions, plot_decisions,
    plot_modules, plot_elbow, plot_soft_threshold,
)
plot_importance(res, kind="beeswarm")     # or "bar" / "both"
plot_stability_elbow(res)                 # per-pool selection curves
plot_potential_interactions(res)          # TreeSHAP interaction heatmap

Benchmarks and a parity harness live in benchmarks/:

python benchmarks/bench_common.py            # config sweep + R comparison + cache
python benchmarks/bench_common.py --out results.csv   # persist results
python benchmarks/parity_in_process.py       # bit-exact parity vs the R backend

docs.title: Parity with the R package
docs.text:
mossyforest (Python) is a bit-exact replica of the R package. Verified in one process on identical data/seed/stack, the two agree exactly:

  • screening survivors identical, selected set identical
  • stability frequencies match to 0.0000
  • signed SHAP matrix bit-identical (max |Δ| = 0.000)

Two things were required for exactness: matching R's survivor-column ordering (original-X order), and a shared per-replicate RNG scheme. float32 (Python) vs float64 (R) is not observable; sklearn trees are float32 internally either way. Re-verify anytime with python benchmarks/parity_in_process.py.

docs.title: License
docs.text: GPL-3.0-or-later.

First release.

  • Module stratified screening, shadow stability selection and a final TreeSHAP pass, matching the R package mossyforest (bit exact on the same data, seed and software stack).
  • The default mtry rule is the standard one: sqrt(p) for classification and p/3 for regression.
  • A UserWarning is raised when an entry of unassigned_modules does not match any module in module_membership.
  • Selection results no longer depend on Python's string hash order, so repeated runs give the same stable set.
  • PyWGCNA is an optional extra (pip install "mossyforest[wgcna]"). It is only needed for wmf() and detect_modules().
  • Supports Python 3.9 to 3.13.

docs.text:
Mossy Forest Feature Selection.

Matches R's mf().

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default X pd.DataFrame or array like (n, p)

Feature matrix. Column names are used when X is a DataFrame.

required y array like (n,)

Outcome. Integer/bool is classification; float is regression.

required module_membership dict, list, ndarray, or pd.Series

Module label per feature. dict: {feature: label}; list/array: aligned with X columns; Series: index = feature names.

required screen_params screen_control

Phase 1 parameters. Default: screen_control().

None select_params select_control

Phase 2 parameters. Default: select_control().

None final_ntree int

Trees in the final prediction RF. Default 500.

500 nodesize int or None

Min terminal node size. None means 1 for classification, 5 for regression.

None num_processors int

Parallel workers for RF fitting. Default 1.

1 max_modsize int

Module size above which blockwise pre reduction is applied. Default 5000.

5000 verbose int

0 = silent; 1 = progress messages; 2 = detailed. Default 1.

1 seed int or None

RNG seed. None = random.

None compute_interactions bool

Retain the single shot RF so the TreeSHAP interaction matrix can be computed lazily on first access (via result.interaction_matrix / detect_interaction / plot_potential_interactions). False disables interactions entirely and frees the retained RF. Default True.

True shap_backend str

"shap" (default) or "fasttreeshap". The latter returns identical values (exact mode) and is faster, but requires Python <=3.11 with numpy<2 / shap<0.46 (fasttreeshap's dependency pins have no Python 3.12+ wheels). On a modern stack keep "shap".

'shap' use_numba bool

Use a Numba JIT mean|SHAP| reduction when Numba is installed. Default False.

False blas_threads int or None

Inner BLAS/OpenMP thread cap during parallel sections. None (default) = auto: capped to 1 when num_processors > 1, unrestricted otherwise.

None screen_cache None, bool, or str/Path

Cache Phase 1 (screening) results, which depend only on X, y, module membership, screen_params, nodesize, seed, max_modsize, and shap_backend, NOT on select_params. Lets tuning / CV runs that vary only select_params skip screening. None/False (default) = no caching; True = in process memory cache (this Python session); str/Path = on disk cache directory (persists across sessions). A cache hit returns byte identical survivors.

None

Returns:

Type Description MossyForestResult

docs.title: mossyforest.screen_control dataclass
docs.text:
Parameters for Phase 1 (per module screening RFE).

Matches R's screen_control().

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default drop_fraction float

Fraction of features eliminated per RFE step. Default 0.25.

0.25 keep_fraction float

Fraction of features retained per module after screening. Default 0.50.

0.5 mtry_factor float

Multiplier applied to the mtry rule. Default 1.0.

1.0 mtry_rule str

How mtry is derived from the feature count p. "auto" (default): sqrt(p) for classification, p/3 for regression. "sqrt": sqrt(p) for both. "p_over_3": p/3 for both.

'auto' min_ntree int

Minimum number of trees per screening forest. Default 500.

500 ntree_factor float

Trees per forest = max(p * ntree_factor, min_ntree). Default 1.0. May be < 1 to reduce the tree count (e.g. 0.5 halves the p scaled term).

1.0

docs.title: mossyforest.select_control dataclass
docs.text:
Parameters for Phase 2 (shadow stability selection).

Matches R's select_control().

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mtry_factor float

mtry multiplier for shadow stability RFs. Default 1.0.

1.0 mtry_rule str

"auto" (default) / "sqrt" / "p_over_3": see screen_control.mtry_rule.

'auto' mtry_on_real bool

How mtry is sized on the AUGMENTED [real | shadow] matrix (2p columns). False (default): mtry = rule(2p). True: mtry = 2 * rule(p_real), so the expected number of REAL features offered per split matches an unaugmented forest (the shadows otherwise dilute real feature sampling by ~half). NOTE: this is a STATISTICAL correction, not a speed optimization; for the "sqrt" rule it is ~1.4x SLOWER (2sqrt(p) > sqrt(2p)); for "p_over_3" it is identical (2(p/3) == 2p/3).

False min_ntree int

Minimum trees per forest. Default 500.

500 ntree_factor float

Trees per forest scaling factor. Default 1.0. May be < 1.

1.0 shadow_mode str

"split": one corr pool + one unassigned pool evaluated separately. "within_module": one shadow run per module. Default "split".

'split' n_reps int

Number of subsample replicates for shadow stability (each draws half the rows without replacement). Default 50.

50 pi_thr float

Stability frequency threshold for the corr pool (used when threshold_mode="pi_thr"). Default 0.60.

0.6 pi_thr_unassigned float or None

Threshold for the unassigned pool. None (default) = automatic elbow detection.

None threshold_mode str

How the per pool selection cutoff is chosen. "pi_thr" (default): correlated pool uses the fixed pi_thr; the unassigned pool uses elbow detection (or pi_thr_unassigned). This matches the R package. "elbow": BOTH pools use the same adaptive elbow rule (unified selection philosophy; a Python only extension not in the R package, so it breaks bit exact R parity when enabled).

'pi_thr' shadow_percentile float

Percentile of the shadow feature distribution used as threshold within each replicate. Default 95.

95.0 unassigned_modules list of str or None

Module names treated as the unassigned pool. None = no split pool.

None use_cfres bool

If True, cross fitted RF residualizes y before the unassigned pool (or per module) stability step. Default False.

False cfres_n_folds int

Cross fitting folds for cfRes residualization. Default 5.

5 cfres_ntree int

Trees per fold RF in cfRes residualization. Default 300.

300 cfres_scope str

"unassigned": cfRes applied only to the unassigned pool (default). "all_modules": per module cfRes applied to every module.

'unassigned' early_stop bool

If True, stop the replicate loop early once selection frequencies converge (changes results by design: fewer effective replicates). Default False.

False early_stop_tol float

Convergence tolerance: stop when the max change in any feature's frequency between consecutive batches is below this. Default 0.01.

0.01 early_stop_check_every int

Replicates per batch; convergence is checked between batches. Also the parallel granularity when early stopping is on. Default 10.

10

docs.title: mossyforest.plot_importance(result, kind='beeswarm', max_display=None, color_bar_title='Feature Value', fill='#3e568a', sort_features=True, show_numbers=True, ax=None)
docs.text:
Feature importance plot: bar or beeswarm.

Ranks the stable features by mean absolute SHAP value. "bar" draws the mean |SHAP| bars, "beeswarm" draws each observation's SHAP value colored by the feature value, and "both" draws the two together. R equivalent: plot_importance().

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default kind "bar", "beeswarm", or "both" 'beeswarm' max_display max number of features shown (None = all) None fill color for the bar chart '#3e568a'

docs.title: mossyforest.plot_signed_importance(result, top_n=None, pos_color='#4393c3', neg_color='#d6604d', ambiguous_color='#bbbbbb', pos_label='increase', neg_label='decrease', ambiguous_label='ambiguous', ax=None)
docs.text:
Diverging bar chart of signed importance = direction × mean|SHAP|.

Magnitude is mean|SHAP|; sign is the global effect direction (from the Spearman correlation between each feature's value and its SHAP value). Bars to the right increase the average predicted outcome, and bars to the left decrease it. Features whose direction is ambiguous (nonmonotone: |Spearman| < 0.1) are greyed out, because a single direction is misleading for them; use a SHAP dependence plot instead. R equivalent: plot_signed_importance().

docs.title: mossyforest.plot_waterfall(result, row_id, row_name=None, max_display=None)
docs.text:
SHAP waterfall plot for one or more observations.

Shows how each feature moves the prediction for one observation up or down from the average prediction. When multiple row_ids are given, SHAP values and feature values are averaged. Row numbers start at 0 here (they start at 1 in R). R equivalent: plot_waterfall().

docs.title: mossyforest.plot_force(result, row_id, row_name=None, max_display=None)
docs.text:
SHAP force plot for one or more observations.

Shows the features that push one observation's prediction above or below the average prediction as a single horizontal bar. When multiple row_ids are given, SHAP values and feature values are averaged. Row numbers start at 0 here (they start at 1 in R). R equivalent: plot_force().

docs.title: mossyforest.plot_decisions(result, highlight=None, just_shap=False, plot_title='Decision Plot', geom_point=False, gradient=('blue', 'red'))
docs.text:
Cumulative SHAP decision plot.

Follows the cumulative SHAP contributions of each observation, feature by feature, from the average prediction to its final prediction. Adapted from the decision plot in the Python shap package. R equivalent: plot_decisions().

docs.title: mossyforest.plot_stability(result, fill='#3e568a', main='Shadow Stability Frequencies', ax=None)
docs.text:
Horizontal bar chart of shadow stability selection frequencies.

Shows how often each stable feature was selected across the shadow stability subsamples, sorted from most to least frequent. R equivalent: plot_stability().

docs.title: mossyforest.plot_stability_elbow(result, col_selected='#3e568a', col_unselected='grey', col_threshold='tomato', col_elbow='#e07b00', show_labels=False, ncol=None, main='Shadow stability selection')
docs.text:
Per pool stability frequency curves with threshold and elbow lines.

Plots the sorted selection frequencies of each pool (correlated and unassigned), with the stability threshold, the elbow rank where one is used, and the selected features in a different color. R equivalent: plot_stability_elbow().

docs.title: mossyforest.plot_elbow(result, main='Elbow Plot of Absolute SHAP Values', xlab='Features', ylab='Mean |SHAP value|', color=True, color_name='Module', module_labels=None)
docs.text:
Scree/elbow plot of mean |SHAP| by stable feature rank.

Ranks the stable features by mean |SHAP| and draws the importance curve, so you can see where importance drops off. Points can be colored by module. R equivalent: plot_elbow().

docs.title: mossyforest.plot_modules(result, main='Module Membership Distribution', xlab='Module', ylab='Proportion of features', module_labels=None)
docs.text:
Stacked bar chart of selected vs not selected proportion per module.

Shows, for each module, the proportion of its features that were selected as stable and the proportion that were not. R equivalent: plot_modules().

docs.title: mossyforest.plot_potential_interactions(result)
docs.text:
Heatmap of mean absolute TreeSHAP pairwise interaction strengths.

Shows the average absolute pairwise TreeSHAP interaction between the stable features. Off diagonal cells are interactions and the diagonal holds the main effects. R equivalent: plot_potential_interactions().

docs.title: mossyforest.plot_soft_threshold(datout, chosen_power, r2_threshold=0.85)
docs.text:
Two panel WGCNA soft threshold diagnostic.

The left panel shows the scale free topology fit (R squared) against the soft threshold power, with a line at r2_threshold. The right panel shows the mean connectivity. Both mark the chosen power. This is the diagnostic that WGCNA's pickSoftThreshold produces; the R package has no plot function for it. datout must have columns "Power", "SFT.R.sq", "mean.k."

docs.title: interaction_matrix property
docs.text:
p×p mean absolute TreeSHAP interaction matrix, computed on first access and cached. Returns None if interactions were disabled (compute_interactions=False) or no stable features were found.

The interaction call is ~p× the cost of regular SHAP, so deferring it until something actually needs it keeps fit() fast.
